result.title: Learning Which Device to Call: Online Tool Grounding for LLM Agents in IoT
result.summary: The Internet of Things (IoT) gives large language model (LLM) agents access to physical observations, but one requested capability is usually offered by several devices, and the agent's plan does not say which one to call. Existing work retrieves relevant tools and checks plan feasibility, without learning which eligible device returns a useful observation. Unlike previous works, we study online tool grounding: binding an already specified tool call to one physical endpoint under service cost and device participation constraints. We propose a framework that learns which physical device should execute each agent-issued call. It formulates selection as a contextual bandit problem and combines adaptive context partitions with hierarchical endpoint trees, so that execution feedback is reused across related requests and devices. Selection balances task success against service cost while respecting device capability, authorization, battery reserves, and availability. Gaussian reward aggregation provides an optional mechanism for protecting individual feedback values. Theoretical results establish a finite-horizon regret bound and differential privacy for released reward statistics under fixed, reward-independent assignments. In a simulated loading-dock workload, the proposed router achieves higher step success and better cost-adjusted service, at lower simulated device energy and latency, than nearest-device, advertised-quality, UCB1, and LinUCB selection.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 IoT 场景下 LLM agent 的在线工具接地：把已指定的工具调用绑定到某个物理设备，用上下文赌博机加自适应上下文划分与分层端点树复用执行反馈，在任务成功与服务成本间权衡，并给出有限时域遗憾界与奖励统计的差分隐私结果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「在多个候选端点中选择哪个能返回有用观测、并权衡成功与成本」的在线决策形式，可能启发 LVR/VLM 推理中 LOOK 阶段视觉证据筛选与获取成本的建模，可供核查；但不涉及 latent 推理状态或生成机制。
